dudley.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Dudley
s1loc: Dudley's emergency food runs largely through Black Country Foodbank, a long-standing local charity in the Trussell network, alongside the Provision House food club and social supermarket and a town-centre St Thomas community foodbank. FareShare West Midlands moves surplus food from the trade out to community groups across the borough, while Dudley CVS supports the wider voluntary sector and Mary Stevens Hospice fundraises through its shops. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks and many small mutual-aid projects all draw volunteers across this Black Country town.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying alongside hospice and air-ambulance fundraising, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Netherton, Sedgley and Kingswinford. We are set up to serve the national charity with shops on every high street and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big buyers and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest group.

Across the Dudley borough, Black Country Foodbank runs its central warehouse in Brierley Hill and crisis sessions in Halesowen, providing emergency food and toiletries. Top Church Training, formed in Brierley Hill in 1997, helps local people reduce isolation and reconnect with community life, while Dudley CVS on Albion Street matches volunteers to projects and the Beacon Centre in Sedgley hosts community groups. From Brierley Hill and Halesowen to Sedgley, small church and centre-based teams of volunteers keep this Black Country network running.

norwich.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Norwich
s1loc: Norwich Foodbank, an independent local charity in the Trussell network, runs emergency food across the city from its Bowthorpe warehouse, while the Norfolk Community Foundation backs the Nourishing Norfolk network of community pantries and social supermarkets. FareShare East Anglia, based over in Ipswich, redistributes surplus food from the trade to breakfast clubs, lunch clubs and refuges across the county.
